extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (agents/attorneys), USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and counsel involved in practitioner discipline
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order approving a settlement resolving a USPTO disciplinary complaint against a registered patent practitioner, stating stipulated facts, legal conclusions, mitigating factors, sanctions, compliance obligations, publication, and procedures for enforcement. It codifies the standards and procedural steps the Office will apply in this settlement context.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Director jurisdiction and authority to approve settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter and the authority to approve the proposed settlement agreement pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements resolving disciplinary action must be approved by the Under Secretary/Director under cited statutory and regulatory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner subject to USPTO Disciplinary Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is an agent registered to practice before the USPTO and is subject to the USPTO Disciplinary Rules set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration subjects practitioners to the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility and discipline under those regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violations charged: 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(b)(5) and 10.23(b)(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting checks that were returned for insufficient funds constitutes violations of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) (engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice) and § 10.23(b)(6) (engaging in conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice law before the Office).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returned checks in connection with client matters pending before the Office constitute conduct triggering these disciplinary provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual basis for discipline: insufficient funds/poor bookkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: From March 2006 through August 2007, Respondent signed and submitted five checks drawn on his business/operating account that were returned for insufficient funds totaling $3,060; Respondent maintained separate client and fee accounts but did not always keep adequate track of monies deposited into and disbursed from his business/operating account or the additional account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to adequately track client/fee/business account funds that results in returned checks to the Office is a factual predicate for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent has been registered as a patent agent for over fifty (50) years and has had no prior disciplinary history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lengthy, clean practice history is a mitigating factor reflected in the agreed-upon discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary sanction structure: stayed suspension and probation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended for twenty-four (24) months from practice before the USPTO; the suspension is immediately stayed and the stay remains in effect during a twenty-four (24) month probationary period; Respondent is permitted to practice during probation unless the stay is lifted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stayed suspension coupled with probation permits continued practice subject to compliance; the stay can be lifted for violations during probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of probation completion on stayed suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the stay of the suspension is not lifted by order of the USPTO Director by the end of the probationary period, Respondent shall not be required to serve the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion of the probation term without lift of the stay renders the suspension unenforced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetary remediation obligation and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent, within thirty (30) days from the date the Final Order is signed, shall make good all returned checks and returned check fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of returned checks and fees is a required condition of the settlement with a 30-day deadline; supporting documentation must follow (see next metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit/corroboration of monetary compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent, within sixty (60) days from the date the Final Order is signed, shall provide an affidavit and other corroborating documentation to the OED Director showing that Respondent has fully complied with the requirement to make good all returned checks and fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentary proof and sworn affidavit are required to demonstrate compliance with monetary remediation within the 60-day deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: CLE / law office management training requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent, within one-hundred and twenty (120) days from the date the Final Order is signed, shall enroll in and complete a three-hour class(es) covering the topic of law office management for the solo and small practitioner that includes specific information on financial bookkeeping and ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must address bookkeeping and ethics for small/solo practice; completion deadline is 120 days from Final Order; supporting affidavit required (see next metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit/corroboration of CLE completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent, within one-hundred and fifty (150) days from the date the Final Order is signed, shall provide an affidavit and other corroborating documentation to the OED Director showing that Respondent has fully complied with the CLE requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sworn verification and documentary evidence of CLE completion required by 150 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause enforcement procedure during probation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director is of the opinion that Respondent, during the probationary period, failed to comply with any provision of the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule, the OED Director shall: (A) issue to Respondent an Order to Show Cause why the stay should not be lifted and Respondent suspended up to twenty-four (24) months; (B) send the Order to the last address of record; and (C) grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure requires issuance, service to record address, and a 15-day response window before further action is taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-response escalation to USPTO Director
rubrics_metrics.description: If after the 15-day period and consideration of any response the OED Director continues to be of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply, the OED Director shall deliver to the USPTO Director the Order to Show Cause, Respondent's response (if any), and evidence causing the OED Director to be of that opinion, and request that the USPTO Director immediately lift the stay and suspend Respondent for up to twenty-four (24) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Escalation packet to USPTO Director triggers request to lift stay and impose suspension; evidentiary showing accompanies the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (URL provided) and publish a notice in the Official Gazette describing the stayed suspension, probation, violations, facts, required conditions (payment and CLE), and mitigating factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final Orders and notices of discipline are posted publicly in the OED Reading Room and Official Gazette and must include the substance specified in the Order's notice text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if stay lifted: compliance, dissemination, dissociation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the stay is lifted and Respondent is suspended: (1) Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; (2) the OED Director shall disseminate information in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; (3) the USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and public key infrastructure (PKI) certificates; (4) Respondent shall not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until reinstated to practice; and (5) Respondent shall not obtain a USPTO customer number or a PKI certificate unless and until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension triggers obligations under §§ 11.58/11.59 and technical/account dissociation and prohibitions on use/obtaining customer numbers and PKI certificates until reinstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited applicability of 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to the suspension identified, 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60 do not apply unless the stay of the suspension is lifted and Respondent is suspended pursuant to the Order's enforcement provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions governing suspension/reinstatement apply only if the stay is actually lifted and suspension imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office's reserved rights to seek further discipline and to use record
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Proposed Settlement Agreement or the Final Order shall prevent the Office from seeking discipline against Respondent in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34 through 11.57 for the misconduct that caused the stay to be lifted and Respondent to be suspended; nor prevent the Office from introducing the record of this proceeding, including the Final Order, (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct, and/or (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding (a) as an aggravating factor and/or (b) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement does not preclude later discipline for the same or similar misconduct and the record may be used as aggravating evidence or rebuttal in future matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs between parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each party is responsible for its own costs arising from the disciplinary matter and settlement implementation.
